keys.explanation: Number of distinct open feedback records asking for this change -- independent voices converging on one problem.
Severity band (average severity, rounded) -- how much the problem hurts when it happens.
The single worst record in the group.
How many different source systems raised it.
Average classifier confidence, as a data-quality tie-breaker only.
Recency of the newest supporting record.

ranking.explanation:
Product actions are ranked lexicographically, not by a weighted score. Only open records count towards a ranking; completed and closed work is excluded so shipped features cannot argue for themselves again. Each key below is applied in order, and the first one that differs decides the position.

**Evidence volume leads, severity follows.** Severity is one model's reading of one piece of text, so a lone severity-4 record is a far weaker signal than several independent records converging on the same problem. Ranking severity first put single-record requests above problems eight people reported. High severity is surfaced instead as its own KPI and filter, where a small number of severe records stays visible without displacing widely-reported ones.

Form Configuration||Structured & repeata.short_summary: Users need to enter multiple related pieces of network data repeatedly, but the form has no table-style input to make this easy and clear.

Form Configuration||Structured & repeata.title: Dynamic Self Service Action
Form Configuration||Structured & repeata.evidence_excerpt: the latter bypasses the regex validations that are applied in the single-container provisioning action
Form Configuration||Structured & repeata.short_summary: Users cannot dynamically add multiple items via a plus button in a form, forcing a separate JSON-list action that skips important validation.

Form Configuration||Structured & repeata.title: Add "Select All" / "Deselect All" for Array-Type Entity Inputs in Self-Service Action Forms
Form Configuration||Structured & repeata.evidence_excerpt: requiring users to manually select each item one by one — which becomes tedious and time-consuming when dealing with large lists
Form Configuration||Structured & repeata.short_summary: Users must manually select each item one by one in large array-type input lists, which is slow and tedious.

Validation & Rules||Input & cross-field.title: Support for Live Regex Validation in String Inputs
Validation & Rules||Input & cross-field.evidence_excerpt: Regex validation used to run live for string inputs, which was a much better experience than waiting until action execution
Validation & Rules||Input & cross-field.short_summary: Regex validation on text fields no longer runs live while typing, forcing users to wait until they submit the action to find out their input is invalid.

Validation & Rules||Input & cross-field.title: Require Object type input property contents, not input itself
Validation & Rules||Input & cross-field.evidence_excerpt: I just want specified properties in the object to be required IF that input is used.
Validation & Rules||Input & cross-field.short_summary: Users cannot mark individual properties inside an object-type action input as required, only the whole object or its property types.

Validation & Rules||Input & cross-field.title: Improved customizations of user inputs validations
Validation & Rules||Input & cross-field.evidence_excerpt: conditional logic like "replica count must be at least 3 when deploying to production", cross-field rules like email confirmation, and meaningful error messages
Validation & Rules||Input & cross-field.short_summary: Builders cannot define complex, conditional, or cross-field validation rules that run in the form before execution, forcing reliance on backend scripts or failed runs to catch bad input.

Invocation & Integrations||Execution age.title: Control which Port Execution Agent deployment process which message with polling streamer
Invocation & Integrations||Execution age.evidence_excerpt: You cannot control which agent processes which message at the moment.
Invocation & Integrations||Execution age.short_summary: Platform admins cannot control which execution agent handles which run when using multiple agents with polling streamer, risking inconsistent filtering logic.

Invocation & Integrations||Execution age.title: Forward everything the Port Execution Agent gets and make it transparent
Invocation & Integrations||Execution age.evidence_excerpt: I mean for it to just forward whatever payload it receives: headers, body, etc.
Invocation & Integrations||Execution age.short_summary: Users want an option to make the Execution Agent fully transparent, forwarding the entire original payload including headers without transformation.

Invocation & Integrations||Execution age.title: In port execution agent allow the agent to have SSL no-verify option when communicating with the remote server
Invocation & Integrations||Execution age.evidence_excerpt: We want to communicate with an internal service without the hassle of handling the self signed certificates
Invocation & Integrations||Execution age.short_summary: Users need a way to let the execution agent skip SSL certificate verification when calling internal services with self-signed certificates.

Form Configuration||Dynamic & dependent.title: Add conditionals based on bool input
Form Configuration||Dynamic & dependent.evidence_excerpt: if input1 true create array to select from in input2 else hide input2
Form Configuration||Dynamic & dependent.short_summary: Users cannot make one form field's visibility or options depend on the value of a boolean field.

Form Configuration||Dynamic & dependent.title: Dropdown input based on API
Form Configuration||Dynamic & dependent.evidence_excerpt: there is no way to offer input selection based on API
Form Configuration||Dynamic & dependent.short_summary: Users cannot populate a dropdown field with options fetched dynamically from an external API.

Form Configuration||Dynamic & dependent.title: Support Calculated Properties in Self-Service Dataset Conditions
Form Configuration||Dynamic & dependent.evidence_excerpt: search conditions cannot be applied to calculated properties in self-service actions
Form Configuration||Dynamic & dependent.short_summary: Action builders cannot filter dropdown or entity selection options in a form using calculated properties as a condition.

Validation & Rules||Expression and JQ ru.title: JQ in Action conditions
Validation & Rules||Expression and JQ ru.evidence_excerpt: it is not possible to use JQ when creating conditions for Day-2 or Delete actions
Validation & Rules||Expression and JQ ru.short_summary: Users cannot use JQ expressions to define conditions for Day-2 or Delete actions, limiting advanced filtering of entities.

Validation & Rules||Expression and JQ ru.title: Reflect invalid JQ results to stakeholders
Validation & Rules||Expression and JQ ru.evidence_excerpt: We should find a way to alert relevant stakeholders to the fact that the calculated value is invalid when it occurs.
Validation & Rules||Expression and JQ ru.short_summary: When a JQ calculation used in an action produces an invalid result, there is no clear way to alert the people who need to know.

Validation & Rules||Expression and JQ ru.title: Support jq version 1.8 in Port
Validation & Rules||Expression and JQ ru.evidence_excerpt: Port currently uses JQ v1.7.1, which does not support functions introduced in v1.8 (e.g., trim, ltrim, rtrim).
Validation & Rules||Expression and JQ ru.short_summary: Port's JQ engine is an older version that lacks newer string functions, forcing users to write workaround regex logic.

Observability & Debugging||Run-history A.title: Action Runs API endpoint improvements
Observability & Debugging||Run-history A.evidence_excerpt: there is not enough ability for filtering of the returned runs, there is no "include" parameter, and the limit is set to max of 1000 runs without ability for pagination
Observability & Debugging||Run-history A.short_summary: The API for retrieving action run history lacks filtering, field inclusion options, and pagination beyond 1000 records.

Observability & Debugging||Run-history A.title: Export Action Run History
Observability & Debugging||Run-history A.evidence_excerpt: Currently Port does not have the ability to export action runs via the UI, only the API.
Observability & Debugging||Run-history A.short_summary: Users cannot export action run history from the UI, only via the API, making it harder to analyze or share run data.

Observability & Debugging||Run-history A.title: Include stable action_id in GET Action Runs API
Observability & Debugging||Run-history A.evidence_excerpt: Exposing the stable action_id in the action runs response will ensure long-term data consistency and reliable analytics.
Observability & Debugging||Run-history A.short_summary: The API for listing action runs does not include a stable identifier for the action, making it hard to reliably track and analyze run data over time.

Permissions & Approvals||Approval audit.title: Audit Log (Runs tab) — Add Approver field and filtering
Permissions & Approvals||Approval audit.evidence_excerpt: Allow filtering by approver directly in the UI, without needing to query the API
Permissions & Approvals||Approval audit.short_summary: The Runs audit log does not show or let users filter by who approved each run, forcing manual API calls to get that information.

Permissions & Approvals||Approval audit.title: API to return action approver details
Permissions & Approvals||Approval audit.evidence_excerpt: It would be beneficial if it could also include the action approver details, such as their name and email.
Permissions & Approvals||Approval audit.short_summary: The API for action runs does not expose who approved the action, such as the approver's name and email.

Permissions & Approvals||Approval audit.title: Expose Approver Context in Runs
Permissions & Approvals||Approval audit.evidence_excerpt: SSA execution context only includes the run creator, not the actual approver
Permissions & Approvals||Approval audit.short_summary: The system does not capture or display who actually approved a request, only who created the run.

Execution Lifecycle||Concurrency, rate l.title: Restrictions on Running Actions in Parallel
Execution Lifecycle||Concurrency, rate l.evidence_excerpt: I want to be able to configure restrictions on running actions in parallel, so that I can control the concurrency of certain tasks within my workflow.
Execution Lifecycle||Concurrency, rate l.short_summary: Admins cannot limit how many times the same action can run at the same time on the same target, risking duplicate or conflicting deployments.

Execution Lifecycle||Concurrency, rate l.title: Disable workflow execute button while execution is in progress
Execution Lifecycle||Concurrency, rate l.evidence_excerpt: users can click the button multiple times, unintentionally triggering duplicate executions
Execution Lifecycle||Concurrency, rate l.short_summary: The action's run button stays clickable while a run is starting, allowing users to accidentally trigger multiple duplicate runs.

Execution Lifecycle||Cancel, stop & resu.title: "Cancel" button for action run
Execution Lifecycle||Cancel, stop & resu.evidence_excerpt: Ability to cancel the execution of an action after triggering it
Execution Lifecycle||Cancel, stop & resu.short_summary: Users cannot stop an action run once it has started, even if it needs to be halted.

Execution Lifecycle||Cancel, stop & resu.title: Cancellation Logic For Self Service Actions
Execution Lifecycle||Cancel, stop & resu.evidence_excerpt: Add a cancel button to self service actions and allow configuration for the cancel button to invoke external communication.
Execution Lifecycle||Cancel, stop & resu.short_summary: Users cannot cancel a running self-service action or trigger an external notification when it is cancelled.

Execution Lifecycle||Completion & result.title: Add the ability to mark run as success/fail for create/update just like it is when using kafka topic
Execution Lifecycle||Completion & result.evidence_excerpt: I would like to have the same ability just with create/update invocation type.
Execution Lifecycle||Completion & result.short_summary: Users cannot manually mark a create/update action run as success or failure the way they can when using Kafka as the backend.

Execution Lifecycle||Completion & result.title: gitlab pipeline trigger action
Execution Lifecycle||Completion & result.evidence_excerpt: the list should contain all Gitlab's possible pipeline statuses: (created, waiting_for_resource, preparing, pending, running, success, failed, canceled, skipped, manual, scheduled)
Execution Lifecycle||Completion & result.short_summary: The action only reports Success or Failure for a GitLab pipeline, even though GitLab pipelines can be in many other states.

Observability & Debugging||Run traceabil.title: Show triggering user in audit logs for entities created via self-service actions
Observability & Debugging||Run traceabil.evidence_excerpt: the audit log shows the entity as being created by Port automation. While the action run itself contains the triggering user's information, that context is not surfaced in the audit log.
Observability & Debugging||Run traceabil.short_summary: Audit logs show entities as created by 'Port automation' instead of showing which user actually triggered the action that created them.

Observability & Debugging||Run traceabil.title: Self-Service Actions to automatically tie affected entities to an action run
Observability & Debugging||Run traceabil.evidence_excerpt: this should be automated when invoking a self service actions - User clicks on an action --> port system gets the entities affected and encodes them with an action runner run_id
Observability & Debugging||Run traceabil.short_summary: Users must manually call an API to link affected entities to an action run instead of this happening automatically.

Discovery, Organization & Reuse||Bulk ac.title: Bulk self-service actions on entities
Discovery, Organization & Reuse||Bulk ac.evidence_excerpt: It would be great to have an option to do bulk actions(day2 and DELETE) on entities
Discovery, Organization & Reuse||Bulk ac.short_summary: Users cannot run day-2 or delete actions on multiple entities at the same time, forcing repeated manual execution.

Discovery, Organization & Reuse||Bulk ac.title: Table & bulk actions
Discovery, Organization & Reuse||Bulk ac.evidence_excerpt: I want to run a single action that references all entities
Discovery, Organization & Reuse||Bulk ac.short_summary: Users want to run a single action against a whole filtered set of entities in a table view, not just one at a time.

Authoring, Testing & Management||API & I.title: Configure action permissions using Port's pulumi provider
Authoring, Testing & Management||API & I.evidence_excerpt: we are not able to configure an action's permissions using the pulumi provider
Authoring, Testing & Management||API & I.short_summary: Users cannot manage an action's permission settings through the Pulumi provider, forcing manual configuration outside of infrastructure-as-code workflows.

Authoring, Testing & Management||API & I.title: Action API viewable per action
Authoring, Testing & Management||API & I.evidence_excerpt: It would be really nice if you could go into a self service action and see a similar view.
Authoring, Testing & Management||API & I.short_summary: Users want to view an action's underlying API/configuration with a working example, similar to the code view available for blueprints.

Context, Targeting & Pre-fill||Embedded.title: Expose Action Form Trigger in Custom Widget/Plugin SDK
Context, Targeting & Pre-fill||Embedded.evidence_excerpt: Add support for opening a self-service action form directly from a custom widget/plugin, without navigating to the Self-Service Actions tab
Context, Targeting & Pre-fill||Embedded.short_summary: Developers cannot launch an action form from a custom widget or plugin without navigating away to the Self-Service Actions tab.

Context, Targeting & Pre-fill||Embedded.title: Triggering a self-service action from somewhere other than the self-service page
Context, Targeting & Pre-fill||Embedded.evidence_excerpt: this link takes the user to the Self-service page (albeit with the correct action modal opened to the form). Completing the form then leaves then on the Self-service page.
Context, Targeting & Pre-fill||Embedded.short_summary: Deep links to an action currently redirect users to the Self-service page instead of opening the action as a modal over the page they were on.

Context, Targeting & Pre-fill||Embedded.title: Configurable automatic execution of self-service actions from Slack
Context, Targeting & Pre-fill||Embedded.evidence_excerpt: Add a configuration option that allows admins to control whether self-service actions triggered via the Slack app can be:
Context, Targeting & Pre-fill||Embedded.short_summary: Admins want the option to let users fully complete and execute self-service actions directly from Slack instead of being redirected to the Port UI.

Authoring, Testing & Management||Editing.title: True Change Detection for Self-service Actions like Data Sources has
Authoring, Testing & Management||Editing.evidence_excerpt: it would be nice if a true diff check was made to see if a change is actually present
Authoring, Testing & Management||Editing.short_summary: The edit dialog always asks to confirm discarding changes, even when nothing was actually changed, causing confusion.

Authoring, Testing & Management||Editing.title: Confirmation Window for Unsaved Changes in Self-service actions GUI Mode
Authoring, Testing & Management||Editing.evidence_excerpt: Currently, this confirmation prompt exists in JSON mode in Self-service action window, but it is missing in GUI mode, which can lead to accidental data loss.
Authoring, Testing & Management||Editing.short_summary: Users editing an action in the visual (GUI) builder can navigate away and lose unsaved changes because no warning is shown, unlike in JSON mode.

Form Configuration||Form layout, section.title: Conditional step in Self-service form
Form Configuration||Form layout, section.evidence_excerpt: I would like to be able to display or not some steps
Form Configuration||Form layout, section.short_summary: Action builders cannot show or hide entire form steps depending on whether a related entity already exists.

Form Configuration||Form layout, section.title: Steps in Port Self-Service Action Form
Form Configuration||Form layout, section.evidence_excerpt: I want the ability to collapse the form into distinct sections such as network configuration, security configuration, and IAM role
Form Configuration||Form layout, section.short_summary: Users want long action forms broken into collapsible sections like network, security, and IAM so they can focus on relevant parts.

Form Configuration||Form layout, section.title: “Execute” Button on the First Step of the Input Window
Form Configuration||Form layout, section.evidence_excerpt: This button will allow users to initiate the action immediately if they do not need to modify any fields in subsequent steps.
Form Configuration||Form layout, section.short_summary: Users must click through every step of a multi-page action form even when they only need to fill in the required fields on the first page.

Orchestration||Shared context & output p.title: Expose GitHub Node Conclusion in Workflow JQ Context
Orchestration||Shared context & output p.evidence_excerpt: the .outputs available to downstream JQ expressions only include workflowRunUrl and workflowRunId, not result, workflowStatus, or any error detail
Orchestration||Shared context & output p.short_summary: When a GitHub Actions step fails, later steps in the same workflow cannot see the failure result or error details, even though that data exists in Port.

Orchestration||Multi-backend & multi-sys.title: I want to be able to use multiple backends for one self service action
Orchestration||Multi-backend & multi-sys.evidence_excerpt: I have to combine these 5 GH actions into one since the SSA can only trigger one backend
Orchestration||Multi-backend & multi-sys.short_summary: Users cannot route a single action to different backend workflows based on the input selected, forcing them to combine multiple backends into one overly complex workflow.

Context, Targeting & Pre-fill||Pre-fill.title: Entity and user/team pickers should allow dynamic filters and defaults
Context, Targeting & Pre-fill||Pre-fill.evidence_excerpt: there's no way to default the team input to, say, the first team in the user's team list
Context, Targeting & Pre-fill||Pre-fill.short_summary: Builders cannot default team, user, or array inputs based on the current user's properties or the entity that triggered the action, forcing manual selection from unfiltered lists.

Execution Lifecycle||Timeouts.title: Configure timeout value for actions
Execution Lifecycle||Timeouts.evidence_excerpt: Ability to configure timeout values for actions within Port so that certain operations, like deploying a service, do not exceed a certain duration.
Execution Lifecycle||Timeouts.short_summary: Users cannot set a maximum time limit for an action run, so long-running operations may run indefinitely.

Invocation & Integrations||Event trigger.title: Event trigger for ALL self-service actions
Invocation & Integrations||Event trigger.evidence_excerpt: it's tied to a specific action rather than ALL actions
Invocation & Integrations||Event trigger.short_summary: Users can only wire an automation trigger to one specific action at a time, not to all actions generally.

Permissions & Approvals||Action visibili.title: Support hiding/displaying self-service actions using dynamic permissions
Permissions & Approvals||Action visibili.evidence_excerpt: the run will be rejected only after sending the self-service action form
Permissions & Approvals||Action visibili.short_summary: Users can see and fill out self-service actions they are not actually permitted to run, only finding out they are rejected after submitting the form.

Orchestration||Intermediate approvals.title: Self Service Action Workflow
Orchestration||Intermediate approvals.evidence_excerpt: Based on that first trigger result, prompt an approval request and based on the approval, invoke another trigger.
Orchestration||Intermediate approvals.short_summary: Users cannot chain multiple execution steps in one action with an approval required between steps before continuing.

Orchestration||Intermediate approvals.title: Support manual approval in the middle of a running action
Orchestration||Intermediate approvals.evidence_excerpt: an action might perform some process and then arrive at another point that requires manual approval
Orchestration||Intermediate approvals.short_summary: Users cannot require a new approval step partway through an already-running action, only before it starts.

Context, Targeting & Pre-fill||Current-u.title: Expose Richer Executing User Context in SSA Backend
Context, Targeting & Pre-fill||Current-u.evidence_excerpt: Passing the User Form .user object to the backend is not safe, as it can be spoofed and allow user impersonation.
Context, Targeting & Pre-fill||Current-u.short_summary: Backends only get a limited set of trusted executing-user data, and using the richer user-submitted data isn't safe because it can be spoofed.

Context, Targeting & Pre-fill||Entity an.title: Associate action with multiple blueprints
Context, Targeting & Pre-fill||Entity an.evidence_excerpt: an action if associated with service overview entity cant be associated with the service blueprint entity - which means a new actions should be created
Context, Targeting & Pre-fill||Entity an.short_summary: Users cannot associate one action with more than one blueprint, forcing them to duplicate actions for each entity type that should trigger the same operation.

Context, Targeting & Pre-fill||Entity an.title: Self service action without requiring blueprint
Context, Targeting & Pre-fill||Entity an.evidence_excerpt: I want the ability to create self-service actions directly within Port without the need for predefined blueprints
Context, Targeting & Pre-fill||Entity an.short_summary: DevOps engineers cannot create a self-service action unless it is tied to a predefined blueprint, limiting flexibility for ad hoc tasks.

Invocation & Integrations||APIs & extern.title: Port Teams Bot Backend
Invocation & Integrations||APIs & extern.evidence_excerpt: We'd like to be able to Install a Port Teams Bot to our Microsoft 365 environment such that the bot can be authorised to communicate with members and channels
Invocation & Integrations||APIs & extern.short_summary: Users want a native Microsoft Teams bot backend so Self-Service Actions can send messages directly to Teams channels and users without building custom infrastructure.

Authoring, Testing & Management||Playgro.title: Entities example for backend playground
Authoring, Testing & Management||Playgro.evidence_excerpt: The examples that are being provided are automatically generated and in some cases are not aligned with the actual data.
Authoring, Testing & Management||Playgro.short_summary: The auto-generated examples in the JQ testing playground don't match real data, making it hard to validate mappings accurately.

Authoring, Testing & Management||Preview.title: Port GitHub action | Support dry run for the Port action for tests
Authoring, Testing & Management||Preview.evidence_excerpt: we would want to have a flag for the port-github-action
Authoring, Testing & Management||Preview.short_summary: Users want a way to run the GitHub Action integration in a test-only mode that validates without triggering real workflow side effects.

Execution Lifecycle||Reliability & trans.title: Retry logic for transient errors in action backends
Execution Lifecycle||Reliability & trans.evidence_excerpt: It would be nice to have the option to have Port manage back pressure and retries of action runs.
Execution Lifecycle||Reliability & trans.short_summary: Users want Port to automatically retry action runs that fail due to temporary backend errors, using backoff, instead of handling retries manually.

Orchestration||Multi-step workflows.title: Multi-step workflows
Orchestration||Multi-step workflows.evidence_excerpt: Chain multiple inputs, approvals, conditions, and actions via automatic triggers or self-service
Orchestration||Multi-step workflows.short_summary: Users want to combine multiple steps, approvals and conditions into a single automated action workflow.

Execution Lifecycle||Retry, rerun & dupl.title: Ability to retry the action from the run page
Execution Lifecycle||Retry, rerun & dupl.evidence_excerpt: Adding a retry action for a run can be nice addition
Execution Lifecycle||Retry, rerun & dupl.short_summary: Users cannot retry a failed action run directly from the run page and must restart the process manually.

Execution Lifecycle||Retry, rerun & dupl.title: Execute another self-service action run with the similar inputs
Execution Lifecycle||Retry, rerun & dupl.evidence_excerpt: We want the ability to execute another run with the same inputs as an existing run, while it is in progress.
Execution Lifecycle||Retry, rerun & dupl.short_summary: Users cannot start a new run with the same inputs as an in-progress run without waiting for it to finish, and the current 'Re-run' wording risks confusion about cancelling the active run.

Authoring, Testing & Management||Drafts,.title: Place action in maintenance mode
Authoring, Testing & Management||Drafts,.evidence_excerpt: It would be great to be able to temporarily disable actions for non-admins.
Authoring, Testing & Management||Drafts,.short_summary: Platform engineers want a way to temporarily disable an action for regular users while it is being updated, without fully deleting or unpublishing it for everyone.
